working_title: Claim-aligned reference models isolate transferable predictive information in hierarchical ecological data
one_sentence_claim: A held-out score gain measures information relative to its reference; aligning that reference with the scientific claim separates identity information from the focal transferable predictive increment.

positioning.odsp_role: supporting implementation for held-out score accounting, frozen experiments and reproducible audits

scientific_principle.name: reference-to-claim alignment
scientific_principle.statement: the comparator defines the predictive information increment being measured; every information layer excluded from the focal transfer claim must already be represented in the reference
scientific_principle.identity_is_focal_information_boundary: when identity itself is the claimed transferable information, an identity-blind pooled reference is appropriate

conceptual_bridge.log_score_information_interpretation: under an oracle conditional distribution, an expected log-score increment corresponds to conditional information; finite-sample ODSP estimates are interpreted as realized held-out predictive increments rather than causal information

required_sequence: problem: predictive improvement is always relative to a reference, but ecological interpretations often name a narrower information source than that reference contrast isolates
principle: define the reference from the scientific claim
known-truth identification: pooled reference credits layer identity or its proxy to context, while claim-aligned conditioning controls false attribution
power: conditioning retains sensitivity to real context information
fresh empirical sign reversal: Palmer Penguins
semantic boundary: Snapshot Serengeti shows pooling is correct when identity is itself the claim
conclusion: reference-to-claim alignment turns predictive skill into an interpretable information contrast

manuscript_structure: Introduction: predictive skill is a contrast, not an attribution
Principle: claim-aligned references define the estimand

panels: identity not focal: condition identity in reference
proxy path: context recovers identity signal

table1.title: Scientific claim determines the lower-information reference

limitations: Stage 2 does not estimate prevalence in published ecological studies
Penguins has three dependence clusters, so mean intervals use CR1 with t(2) and superpopulation certainty is limited
BOP has four species clusters and is descriptive for the present paper
score decomposition attributes predictive information, not biological causality
the scientific hierarchy must be declared; software cannot infer the correct claim
